messages:
deploybot: Canary deploy failed: 2/5 unhealthy. Step=canary-deploy. Reason=cache restore throttled by artifact storage (rate_limited). Retrying automatic backoff...

alex: saw this. looks like GCS per-project throttle on cache restores. can we fallback to uncached build for canary? @cheng any objections? :eyes:

maya: canary latency also spiked and a couple e2e tests timed out. if we let this run it might block promotion. prefer quick fix > full rollback.

cheng: we did pin runtime to v3.2.1 in this release. pipeline uses `restore_cache` which is hammering our storage bucket with parallel fetches. two options: 1) skip cache for canary job, 2) limit restore to essential layers only. skipping is fastest to unblock.

priya: change window until 18:00 PT. i agree avoid full rollback if we can patch pipeline quickly. alex, can you open a fast PR to skip cache for canary? i'll hold promotion until canary green.

alex: on it. PR will add `skip_cache: true` to `canary-build` job and reduce parallel fetches for other jobs. opening now.

deploybot: PR <https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4321|#4321> opened by alex. Auto-run: canary rebuild will trigger on merge. :white_check_mark:

cheng: note: skipping cache will increase canary build time (~3x), but acceptable for canary. also we should set artifact fetch retry to 5 with exponential backoff instead of 2. snippet:
```yaml
jobs:
  canary-build:
    steps:
      - restore_cache: {name: infra-layers, skip_cache: true}
      - build: ...
    retries:
      fetch_artifact: {retries: 5, backoff: exponential}
```

maya: ack. we need a short line in release notes about this: "canary uses uncached build temporarily; expect higher build times/latency". i'll add to the draft.

priya: decision: do NOT rollback global release. HOLD promotion. Patch deployed to pipeline (skip cache) -> re-run canary. If canary fails again by 16:30 PT, execute rollback plan. :clock3:

alex: merged PR 4321, re-run started. logs show restore step skipped, building layers from scratch. first unit tests running.

deploybot: Canary: build finished, tests passed. 3/5 nodes healthy. Observed p90 latency +80ms vs baseline while cache disabled. Marking canary as "observation" for 1h.

cheng: i'll follow up with infra to request temporary higher cache quota and add rate-limiting client-side to reduce burst. longer-term: shard caches per-team to avoid cross-project throttle.

maya: updating release notes draft and change-window doc with a known-issue bullet. Also adding note to engineering slack: `Known transient canary latency while cache disabled`.

priya: thanks. leaving promotion blocked until end of observation window. if no regressions, we promote and add a follow-up ticket to restore cache after quota change. closing thread when promotion done. :thumbsup:
